// Generated by the Codename One Python transpiler.
package @PACKAGE@;

import com.codename1.backend.Web;
import com.codename1.backend.WebClient;
import com.codename1.python.runtime.PyHttp;
import java.io.ByteArrayOutputStream;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.InputStream;
import java.io.OutputStream;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Iterator;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;

/// The HTTP client `requests` and `httpx` use in a backend build: the
/// backend's own, over libcurl. Generated only into a backend build -- an
/// application's is the network manager, which the backend's class library
/// does not have.
///
/// Redirects are followed here, not by the transport, so that
/// `allow_redirects` means what it does under CPython and the response
/// carries the URL it really came from. The transport's own policy depends
/// on the headers sent, and `requests` always sends some.
final class BackendHttp extends PyHttp {
    /// What `requests` allows before giving up (`requests.models.DEFAULT_REDIRECT_LIMIT`).
    private static final int MAX_REDIRECTS = 30;

    private BackendHttp() {
    }

    static void install() {
        if (!PyHttp.installed()) {
            PyHttp.install(new BackendHttp());
        }
    }

    @Override
    public Response send(String method, String url, String[] headers, byte[] body, int timeoutMillis,
            boolean followRedirects) throws IOException {
        WebClient client = new WebClient();
        try {
            if (timeoutMillis > 0) {
                client.setConnectTimeoutMillis(timeoutMillis);
                client.setReadTimeoutMillis(timeoutMillis);
            }
            String[] sent = headers;
            for (int hops = 0;; hops++) {
                Response r = once(client, method, url, sent, body);
                String location = followRedirects ? header(r, "Location") : null;
                int status = r.status;
                if (location == null || (status != 301 && status != 302 && status != 303
                        && status != 307 && status != 308)) {
                    return r;
                }
                if (hops >= MAX_REDIRECTS) {
                    throw new IOException("Exceeded " + MAX_REDIRECTS + " redirects.");
                }
                String next = resolve(url, location);
                // As requests does: 303 becomes a GET, and so does a POST
                // answered 301 or 302; the body goes with the method.
                if (status == 303 && !"HEAD".equals(method)
                        || (status == 301 || status == 302) && "POST".equals(method)) {
                    method = "GET";
                    body = null;
                    sent = without(sent, "Content-Length", "Content-Type", "Transfer-Encoding");
                }
                // Credentials stay with the host they were meant for.
                if (!host(next).equalsIgnoreCase(host(url))) {
                    sent = without(sent, "Authorization", "Cookie", null);
                }
                url = next;
            }
        } finally {
            client.close();
        }
    }

    private static Response once(WebClient client, String method, String url, String[] headers,
            byte[] body) throws IOException {
        List lines = new ArrayList();
        for (int i = 0; i + 1 < headers.length; i += 2) {
            lines.add(headers[i] + ": " + headers[i + 1]);
        }
        boolean hasBody = body != null && body.length > 0;
        Web.Exchange ex = client.open(method, url, lines, hasBody ? body.length : 0);
        try {
            if (hasBody) {
                OutputStream out = ex.getRequestBody();
                out.write(body);
                out.close();
            }
            int status = ex.getStatus();
            if (status <= 0) {
                throw new IOException("no response from " + url);
            }
            List all = new ArrayList();
            Map values = ex.getHeaderValueMap();
            for (Iterator it = values.keySet().iterator(); it.hasNext();) {
                String name = String.valueOf(it.next());
                Object v = values.get(name);
                if (v instanceof List) {
                    List l = (List) v;
                    for (int i = 0; i < l.size(); i++) {
                        all.add(name);
                        all.add(String.valueOf(l.get(i)));
                    }
                }
            }
            InputStream in = ex.getResponseBody();
            ByteArrayOutputStream data = new ByteArrayOutputStream();
            byte[] buf = new byte[8192];
            for (int n = in.read(buf); n >= 0; n = in.read(buf)) {
                data.write(buf, 0, n);
            }
            in.close();
            return new Response(status, reason(status), url,
                    (String[]) all.toArray(new String[all.size()]), data.toByteArray());
        } finally {
            ex.close();
        }
    }

    private static String header(Response r, String name) {
        for (int i = 0; i + 1 < r.headers.length; i += 2) {
            if (r.headers[i].equalsIgnoreCase(name)) {
                return r.headers[i + 1];
            }
        }
        return null;
    }

    private static String[] without(String[] headers, String a, String b, String c) {
        List kept = new ArrayList();
        for (int i = 0; i + 1 < headers.length; i += 2) {
            String n = headers[i];
            if (n.equalsIgnoreCase(a) || n.equalsIgnoreCase(b) || c != null && n.equalsIgnoreCase(c)) {
                continue;
            }
            kept.add(n);
            kept.add(headers[i + 1]);
        }
        return (String[]) kept.toArray(new String[kept.size()]);
    }

    /// `location` against `base`: absolute, scheme-relative, rooted or relative.
    static String resolve(String base, String location) {
        if (location.indexOf("://") > 0) {
            return location;
        }
        int scheme = base.indexOf("://");
        String prefix = base.substring(0, scheme + 1);
        if (location.startsWith("//")) {
            return prefix + location;
        }
        int pathStart = base.indexOf('/', scheme + 3);
        String origin = pathStart < 0 ? base : base.substring(0, pathStart);
        if (location.startsWith("/")) {
            return origin + location;
        }
        String path = pathStart < 0 ? "/" : base.substring(pathStart);
        int cut = path.indexOf('?');
        if (cut >= 0) {
            path = path.substring(0, cut);
        }
        return origin + path.substring(0, path.lastIndexOf('/') + 1) + location;
    }

    private static String host(String url) {
        int scheme = url.indexOf("://");
        int end = url.indexOf('/', scheme + 3);
        return (end < 0 ? url.substring(scheme + 3) : url.substring(scheme + 3, end));
    }

    /// The standard reason phrase; libcurl does not hand back the server's.
    static String reason(int status) {
        switch (status) {
            case 200: return "OK";
            case 201: return "Created";
            case 202: return "Accepted";
            case 204: return "No Content";
            case 206: return "Partial Content";
            case 301: return "Moved Permanently";
            case 302: return "Found";
            case 303: return "See Other";
            case 304: return "Not Modified";
            case 307: return "Temporary Redirect";
            case 308: return "Permanent Redirect";
            case 400: return "Bad Request";
            case 401: return "Unauthorized";
            case 403: return "Forbidden";
            case 404: return "Not Found";
            case 405: return "Method Not Allowed";
            case 406: return "Not Acceptable";
            case 408: return "Request Timeout";
            case 409: return "Conflict";
            case 410: return "Gone";
            case 413: return "Content Too Large";
            case 415: return "Unsupported Media Type";
            case 422: return "Unprocessable Content";
            case 429: return "Too Many Requests";
            case 500: return "Internal Server Error";
            case 501: return "Not Implemented";
            case 502: return "Bad Gateway";
            case 503: return "Service Unavailable";
            case 504: return "Gateway Timeout";
            default: return "";
        }
    }
}
